## 07 · Revocation cascade
The workflow that makes “withdraw at any time” real.

Append-only revocation entry → stamp live consents → **kill share tokens** → stop reminders → optional erasure → receipt.

Each step always emits a row (sentinel `__noop__` when there is nothing to do) so the cascade can never half-complete.

nodes.name: Gather affected records
nodes.notes: One read of everything the cascade has to touch.

nodes.name: Plan cascade
nodes.notes: Decides everything up front, so the receipt matches what actually happens.

nodes.name: Doc · revocation entries
nodes.notes: The ledger grows; nothing in it is ever rewritten.

nodes.name: Doc · revoke share tokens
nodes.notes: The single most important write in the system. After this, a facility presenting the token to workflow 03 is refused.

nodes.name: Doc · stop nudges & redact
nodes.notes: Redaction keeps the assessment row (so counts and fairness metrics survive) but removes every answer value.

nodes.name: Doc · erase contact details
nodes.notes: Contact details are the only link to a person, so erasure starts here.

nodes.name: Build receipt
nodes.notes: The user gets a specific, checkable list. Vague reassurance is what erodes trust in exactly this kind of service.
